correctness.rationale: The proof is exact. The iid squared-distance identity reduces both sampling laws to centroids and second moments. \(\operatorname{Dirichlet}(1,1,1)\) barycentric moments give the interior formula; an edge-length-weighted mixture of uniform segment moments gives the boundary formula. Subtraction is checked both in side lengths and classical triangle invariants. Strict positivity follows from an explicit positive polynomial in \(x=s-a\), \(y=s-b\), \(z=s-c\). The accompanying symbolic replay verifies all algebraic reductions; no finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The \(p=2\) case is a natural structural test of the current boundary-versus-interior moment conjecture. Recent work covers arbitrary triangles at \(p=1\) and all \(p\) only under centroid conditions that generic triangles fail. The result gives an exact quantitative gap in \(s,R,r\) for every triangle, so it is more informative than a sign check and can serve as a benchmark for broader moment comparisons.
